title: Stable influence from norm contraction
statement: Let $n\in\mathbb{N}$, let $P$ be a finite product probability space with $n$ coordinates, and let $q,\rho\in\mathbb{R}$ satisfy $q\ge 2$ and $\rho\ge 0$. Let $f$ be a real-valued function on the outcome space taking values in $\{-1,1\}$, and let $i$ be a coordinate. If $\|T_{\sqrt{\rho}}L_i f\|_{2,P}\le\|L_i f\|_{q/(q-1),P}$, then $\rho I_i^{(\rho)}(f)\le I_i(f)^{2-2/q}$.
hypotheses_covered: $n\in\mathbb{N}$ and a finite product probability space $P$ with $n$ coordinates
$f$ is real-valued and takes values in $\{-1,1\}$
replaced: Let $P$ be a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses and outcome space $\Omega=\prod_i\Omega_i$, $q\ge2$, $\rho\ge0$, $f:\Omega\to\{-1,1\}$, and a coordinate $i$. If $\|T_{\sqrt\rho}L_if\|_{2,P}\le\|L_if\|_{q/(q-1),P}$, then $\rho I_i^{(\rho)}(f)\le I_i(f)^{2-2/q}$. For a real function $h$ on $\Omega$, use $E_Uh(x)=\mathbb E_P[h(X)\mid X_U=x_U]$ for $X\sim P$ and $U\subseteq[n]$; $h_S=\sum_{U\subseteq S}(-1)^{|S|-|U|}E_Uh$ for $S\subseteq[n]$ (the Hoeffding--Efron--Stein components); $T_a h=\sum_{S\subseteq[n]}a^{|S|}h_S$ for every real rate $a$; $\|h\|_{p,P}=(\mathbb E_P|h|^p)^{1/p}$ for $p>0$; $L_i h=h-E_{[n]\setminus\{i\}}h$; $I_i(h)=\mathbb E_P(h-E_{[n]\setminus\{i\}}h)^2$; $I_i^{(a)}(h)=\sum_{S\ni i}a^{|S|-1}\mathbb E_Ph_S^2$ for $a\in\mathbb R$. The powers indexed by subset cardinalities are natural powers, including $0^0=1$.
